summary:
Astro-Care: Keeping Astronauts Healthy Beyond Earth is a health monitoring software solution developed by Team Kyberverein for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the theme Next Frontiers. It addresses the healthcare challenges faced by astronauts during long-duration space missions, where communication delays, limited medical assistance, and harsh space environments make real-time healthcare difficult.

Astronauts face several health risks, including radiation exposure, bone and muscle loss, immune system changes, cardiovascular problems, and mental health challenges caused by isolation and confinement. Existing healthcare tools are often fragmented, making it difficult to identify early warning signs.

Our solution, Astro-Health, is an autonomous, offline-first health monitoring application that collects, tracks, analyzes, and alerts astronauts about potential health risks. It integrates wearable devices, daily health check-ins, exercise records, and environmental data to establish individual health baselines and detect unusual changes.

Its key features include daily health check-ins, wearable integration, bone and muscle monitoring, mental wellness assessment, radiation exposure tracking, and smart alerts with personalized recommendations and medical guidance.
details:
Project Title: Astro-Care: Keeping Astronauts Healthy Beyond Earth

Project Description:

Astro-Care is an autonomous health monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It tracks vital signs, sleep, mental wellness, physical activity, bone and muscle health, and radiation exposure. Using wearable data and daily health check-ins, it identifies potential health risks, generates smart alerts, and provides personalized recommendations. Its offline-first design ensures reliable monitoring even when communication with Earth is delayed. The project aims to improve astronaut safety and support future Moon and Mars missions.

Key Features:

  • Real-time health monitoring
  • Wearable device integration
  • Bone and muscle tracking
  • Mental wellness monitoring
  • Radiation exposure tracking
  • Smart alerts and personalized guidance
  • Offline-first operation

Expected Impact: Safer, healthier, and more independent astronauts during long-duration space exploration, with potential applications in remote healthcare.Project Title: Astro-Care: Keeping Astronauts Healthy Beyond Earth
